item.title: How Agentic Coding Drives Bitcoin Adoption
item.dc:creator: Roy Sheinfeld
item.content:encoded:
Fifteen years ago, Marc Andreessen wrote that “software is eating the world.” It has. But since 2025, AI has been eating software. Agentic coding, notably since the release of Claude Code, has been radically altering the shape of software development. Projects that used to occupy a team of developers for weeks can now be completed by a single builder in an afternoon at a minuscule fraction of the cost.

Bitcoin is no exception. Just as hardware stores are good indicators of construction activity, we at Breez make tools for devs building apps with the help of coding agents and, increasingly, for agents building apps on behalf of humans. Therefore, we see the trends just before they hit the market.

The trend we are currently observing and servicing is an unprecedented increase in the quantity of new implementations, the range of apps implementing bitcoin, and the speed with which they hit the market.

In short, AI and bitcoin are feeding each other’s rise.

Quantitative Transformation: Recent and Huuuge

Some changes, like the Industrial Revolution, start gradually and progress incrementally, so it’s hard to date when they really began. The advent of agentic coding is not like that. Claude Code was released as a research preview in February 2025 and became generally available three months later. These dates stand out like beacons in the history of bitcoin’s integration into apps, and they match perfectly with our internal data.

The most salient internal data we have is requests from potential partners. Two years ago, we were fielding a steady stream of inquiries from developers who wanted to add bitcoin to their apps with our best-in-class SDK. How many? Enough to keep us busy. Or so we thought.

Once Claude Code hit the scene, our steady upward curve pulled back on the stick and hit the afterburner. The volume of inquiries went up 14x, 1400%, ten-ex and a bunch more. Agentic coding has changed the entire development workflow, and since we build tools for developers, our world changed with it.

The good news is that we were well equipped to deal with it. By the time agentic coding was becoming a thing, our SDK had been helping businesses add bitcoin to their apps for a couple of years already. We had also just released the implementation leveraging Spark, which is the most scalable tool we’ve ever released. Despite the radically increasing demand, it stood as solid as a pyramid and purred like a kitten under the increased volume.

Qualitative Transformation: Here Comes Everybody

Beyond the speed and scale of the change, we’ve also noticed two momentous changes in who is inquiring about new partnerships. First, with the advent of Claude Code we started seeing far more inquiries from people who had little to no experience with bitcoin.

Prior to 2025, by far the majority of potential partners were orange-blooded bitcoin aficionados, crypto enthusiasts for whom bitcoin was the OG of cryptocurrency, and fintechies who saw bitcoin as just another asset class that belongs in every diversified portfolio. But around the beginning of last year, we started fielding requests from developers building apps from verticals we had barely contemplated. We were getting questions about whether the Breez SDK would work with fitness apps, whether users could send each other money with our SDK in messenger apps, how it would fare as a means of payment in an eSIM service for travel, could the team behind a mushroom-identification app please get a little integration support? (Answers: yes; of course; brilliantly; sure.)

The fungus vertical is one few people think about, but which does indicate that one’s SDK has obtained a certain reach. Within a few weeks, our TAM had expanded from maybe one and a half verticals to all the verticals. It’s the “more apps with Lightning” we had been predicting.

The second momentous change in the source of the new inquirers was that many were not even human. For example, we’re now regularly fielding requests from coding agents themselves, who are writing on behalf of the companies deploying them. It comes as no surprise that machines are now working with our SDK. It’s a development kit, and they’re designed to help develop software. But the scale is a surprise. Agents and the people using them obviously prefer bitcoin, as our data indicates, but why?

AI Tends Towards Bitcoin Because It Has To

Both coding agents and human developers building with them need bitcoin, but for slightly different reasons.

Many of our new human partners prefer bitcoin for the speed. By the time they’ve opened an account at their local bank and figured out how to deal with cross-border transfers, they probably could have already started turning a profit with bitcoin or stablecoins. Getting ready to accept fiat payments takes weeks, maybe months. With our SDK, you could have become able to send or receive bitcoin, USDT, and USDC from anywhere in the world in about the time it’s taken you to read this far. Take it for a test drive with Glow.

For coding agents, speed is just one advantage. Even more important is the fact that bitcoin is permissionless. Agents can build an app and set up its global monetization, letting users send money anywhere at any time, without obtaining anyone’s permission or signing a single form. Bitcoin lets agents build without humans and their petty rules and borders getting in the way.

This is a radical departure from the status quo. Conventional payments are built around a world of permission, of humans telling other humans what’s allowed, where, when, and under what conditions. It was a fine system for the days of COBOL and gold reserves. But it is not even wrong when it comes to a world of rapid, global, agentic software development.

Bitcoin is agnostic about whether the code of its current owner and user is composed of DNA base pairs or weights in a neural net. AI needs bitcoin because bitcoin accommodates AI.

Growth Is Great, Organic or Otherwise

Agentic coding is changing bitcoin by vastly expanding the range of apps integrating it into their use cases and by massively accelerating that integration. Conversely, bitcoin is changing AI by giving it a radically new use case: helping developers help users to start moving and harvesting value with unprecedented speed and without the permission and restrictions of traditional financial instruments.

There was a time in recent memory when people would ask us whether our tech actually worked. Now they ask how fast they can integrate it. Except that it’s often their coding agents asking us, and the agents answer by implementing bitcoin in seconds. Bitcoin is important infrastructure in the era of coding agents, and infrastructure is what conquers the world. We’re past ideology and orange pills. We’re now at the stage of electrical sockets and subsea cables: parts of the world everybody uses but few really think about (or need to).

But for all this rapid change, the fundamental means and ends remain the same. The ends we’re pursuing are just permissionless, global money for all of us. The way to achieve it hasn’t changed either: build products that provide value and make them as simple, seamless, and intuitive as possible. As ever, the user experience is the key, and that remains true even if machines are the ones designing and building it.

How Agentic Coding Drives Bitcoin Adoption was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: The Breez SDK: Class of Q3 2026
item.dc:creator: Danny S
item.content:encoded:
In Crossing the Chasm, Geoffrey Moore describes the pattern of early adopters on the near side of the chasm, who try something because it’s new, and pragmatists on the far side, who only move when it solves a problem they already have. For most of its life, bitcoin has been a nifty technology on the near side.

The Class of Q3 2026 lives on the far side. It includes a hardware wallet that finally spends, a messenger where a payment is just another message, an app to pay utility bills in Romania, a film platform that pays directors by the second, a trailhead coffee shop that knocks ten percent off. None of them are “selling” bitcoin. They’re delivering something people already want, with instant, non-custodial bitcoin built-in, all powered by the Breez SDK.

Without further ado, here’s your Class of Q3 2026.

BIF Wallet

A bitcoin wallet inside Telegram, built for Persian speakers

BIFWallet is part of the BIF Ecosystem, built around Bitcoin Rah-e Azadi, a Persian-language community whose name translates to “Bitcoin Is Freedom.” The goal is to go beyond bitcoin education and give Persian speakers practical tools for everyday life.

BIFWallet is a non-custodial wallet built directly into Telegram, in Persian, so there’s nothing new to install. The BIF package also includes BIFp2p (a peer-to-peer trading bot) and BIFChat (the community group), which combines education, community, payments, and exchange in one place. It’s bitcoin freedom powered by Breez.

BitBox

Cold storage, instant spending

If you’ve held bitcoin for any length of time, you’ve probably considered a BitBox. Designed and built in Switzerland with fully open-source firmware, it has reliably kept users’ bitcoin on lockdown, which also made that money hard to spend. So BitBox users did what most hardware wallet users do: keep their savings on the device and use a second app for spending, with yet another seed phrase to look after.

Now saving and spending both live in the BitBoxApp. Savings stay secured in your BitBox while a spending wallet on your phone handles everyday payments. You can top the wallet up from the device whenever you want. The spending wallet is derived from users’ existing BitBox backups, so there are no new recovery words to write down. The Breez-powered public beta is already on mobile for all BitBox hardware wallets.

Bitcoin Pixel

Paint by numbers, pay in sats

Remember the Million Dollar Homepage? Bitcoin Pixel is its collaborative, pay-as-you-go successor. Pick a banner, draw or import your artwork, place it on the live canvas, and pay a few sats to make it stick. No account, no sign-up, and pixels are repaintable, so the canvas keeps changing as new people paint over the old. Anyone can open a banner, set their own pricing rules, and get paid every time someone paints on it, straight to their own wallet. A full replay shows every change back to the first pixel. Instant bitcoin, powered by Breez.

Bro

Scan a bill, pay in bitcoin

Bro is an open, peer-to-peer way to pay real-world bills in Brazil and across Latin America with bitcoin, with no accounts, no KYC and no central server. Scan a bill or paste a PIX code and pay in bitcoin. A provider on the network pays the bill in local currency and uploads encrypted proof, and once you confirm it’s paid, escrow releases the sats to them. Users skip the exchange, providers buy bitcoin without KYC and earn a 3% fee, and the orders are coordinated over Nostr by coordinators anyone can run. Every user gets a non-custodial wallet powered by the Breez SDK, and Bro already handles PIX, Boleto and TED in Brazil, plus CoDi, PromptPay, Transf 3.0 and Bre-B.

BTCfactura

The electric bill, paid in bitcoin

Bitcoin will have made it when people think of it as an unglamorous utility, like electricity and SWIFT. Well, BTCfactura lets people in Romania pay their electricity, gas, water, and internet bills in bitcoin, across 245+ providers, which is about as unglamorous and useful as it gets.

This handy app runs on a self-hosted BTCPay Server through its own fork of Flint, the open-source plugin from Seth For Privacy, that gives every merchant their own wallet with automatic on-chain sweeps. The Breez SDK sits underneath, so the payment clears and the customer gets a receipt in seconds.

BuhoGO

A community-built wallet that speaks bitcoin

BuhoGO is a community-built, non-custodial bitcoin wallet for the web and Android. Either connect it to a node you already run through Nostr Wallet Connect or LNbits, or use the built-in wallet powered by the Breez SDK, and this one app will handle both. The wallet lives on your device, not on anyone’s server, and the code is open on GitHub for anyone who wants to build on it or for it.

Coinsnap

One wallet, both sides of the counter

Most bitcoin wallets specialize in serving either the customer or the shop. Coinsnap, which has built bitcoin payment tools for merchants since 2023, now has one non-custodial app for both: a merchant accepts bitcoin at the register with the same wallet a customer uses to pay, and online shops settle straight into it through a Lightning address set up in the Coinsnap Merchant Dashboard.

Over 1,200 people are using it already, mostly in German-speaking countries, but Coinsnap is stoked to be rolling it out across Europe, with instant bitcoin powered by the Breez SDK.

Freedomia

Spend your bitcoin in seconds

Freedomia issues a virtual Visa card with no KYC that can be loaded with bitcoin, USDT, USDC, and a range of other currencies. The current version of Freedomia was born of necessity, and it went live in no time. When their previous swap provider went down, the team rebuilt bitcoin deposits on the Breez SDK in about 23 hours: API key received at 10pm, live by 9pm the next day. Today a deposit is spendable in under 40 seconds, and it works anywhere you can spend with Visa.

Freeport.Network

A marketplace with no company in the middle

Freeport is a peer-to-peer marketplace for rides, services, and goods, and it’s built on Nostr. There is no company in the middle, no server to run, no commission, and no account: just people trading gigs for money without any middleman.

The whole app runs from a single HTML file you can download, with an instant bitcoin wallet running on the Breez SDK. Ridesharing is the first use case, and the driver gets paid at the curb with no intermediary getting between the passengers. The next stop on their roadmap is peer-to-peer chat with instant payments.

IndeeHub

Every second watched is a sat paid

Before founding IndeeHub, Zack Mahoney spent half his career in front of the camera and half behind it, so he knows how the video business works. Subscriptions, he says, create distorted incentives that plague the industry, leading to dissatisfaction amongst audiences and filmmakers alike.

Blazing a new path, IndeeHub pays filmmakers straight from viewers’ wallets for every second their films are watched, and every viewer holds the keys to their own wallet, letting them watch, tip, or use it as an everyday bitcoin wallet. IndeeHub is in open beta with content by award-winning independents including Dirty Coin, The Ataxian, and Hummingbird.

Minmo

Bitcoin plumbing for African businesses

In Africa, bitcoin on- and off-ramps are often actual human agents who help people buy and sell the bitcoin they need to transact, and Minmo builds the infrastructure that lets businesses offer those services. Leveraging the Breez SDK, Minmo offers three tools, all available through its APIs: hosted wallets for business operations, escrow that holds and releases bitcoin under agreed conditions so swaps between strangers go smoothly, and an OTC desk for pricing, liquidity and settlement.

The beauty of bitcoin is its universal applicability, and the beauty of the Breez SDK is adapting that universality to any number of local and regional particularities. Together, Minmo and Breez are fitting the world’s best financial product to the needs of African businesses, and the fit is only going to get better with the stablecoin balances and exportable, accounting-grade records they’re busy building.

PPQ.AI

Frontier AI is sats away

PPQ.AI puts the leading AI models behind one pay-as-you-go interface with no registration and no subscription: send a few sats, get the answer you need, get on with your life. Bitcoin is what makes paying-by-the prompt possible, and PPQ.AI runs its revenue-share payouts through the Breez SDK, so the partners who bring usage to the platform get paid the moment it happens.

Radar Chat

Chat and send sats to anyone, anywhere

Radar is an end-to-end encrypted messenger from the team behind Cake Wallet, with instant, non-custodial bitcoin built in. It’s built on Signal, so your contacts are already loaded, and the payment is a message that settles instantly and stays encrypted along with everything else in the thread.

There is no wallet to open and no address to copy. If you lose the phone, a phone number can restore both the account and the wallet. “[The Breez SDK] was fast. No hassle. Easy to use, easy to set up,” says Vikrant Sharma, Radar’s CEO. Just like Radar Chat.

Shosho

Watch it, zap it, buy it

Shosho is a live-streaming marketplace, where fans back the creators they watch and shop their sales without ever leaving the stream. Their latest release adds a non-custodial bitcoin wallet, so viewers can zap a creator mid-show, pay anyone in their contacts, top up streaming server credits, and pay for what they buy, all from the same balance. It’s live now on Android and iOS, powered by Breez.

Taro Wallet by DFX

Neutral on everything except your keys

Taro Wallet is DFX’s open-source, non-custodial bitcoin wallet, and it plugs straight into DFX’s regulated Swiss on- and off-ramp. It features on-chain savings, instant bitcoin, multisig security, and sending and receiving in CHF or EUR, all in one app. Of course, DFX never holds users’ funds.

DFX serves more than 30,000 customers and has processed over $100 million in transactions, and its OpenCryptoPay network already takes bitcoin in 137 SPAR stores across Switzerland. With instant bitcoin from the Breez SDK, Taro Wallet is bringing instant payments to everyday grocery shopping in the Alps.

Trails Coffee

Proof of brew

Trails Coffee is a boutique coffee shop located at a trailhead in Anmore, British Columbia, forty minutes from Vancouver, where they roast the trademark Buntzen Blend on site every week. Since opening in January 2026, Trails has built its own app, where every customer gets a bitcoin wallet and their own Lightning address, and orders paid in bitcoin get ten percent off.

Buying a cup of coffee has long been the litmus test for bitcoin’s utility as an everyday currency. With Trails Coffee and the Breez SDK, the moment has come, and it’s delicious.

The Breez SDK: Class of Q3 2026 was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Introducing Glow: Experience What’s Possible with the Breez SDK
item.dc:creator: Danny S
item.content:encoded:
Introducing Glow: Experience What’s Possible

When you give developers an effortless DX, it doesn’t just make building easier, it strips away all limitations between them and their vision. It’s that newfound freedom that pushes these teams to craft an exceptional UX, one that completely redefines what’s possible for builders and users alike. The result isn’t just a better bitcoin app, it’s an everyday app that’s intuitive from the first tap, feature-rich without feeling overwhelming, and a delight to use.

Introducing Glow.

Glow is a bitcoin app for everyone. Everyday users can open Glow and use it for everyday payments, whether in bitcoin or USD. But it’s great for developers too. We built it so that they can look under the hood, take it apart, and see how easy it is to implement features with the straightforward API of the Breez SDK.

Most developers exploring Breez and the possibilities of bitcoin probably already have ideas of what they’re looking to build, they just need a glimpse of what’s possible and what they need to realize it. And that’s where Glow glows shines. It’s easy to use, it’s easy to understand, and easy to make your own.

Everything a Bitcoin App Needs

The API of the Breez SDK includes all the features that a bitcoin app needs to lead in any vertical, and Glow shows you how it’s done. These features include:

  • Passkey Login: Seedless onboarding and restore, with no recovery phrase necessary. Face and fingerprint unlock both work, synced through iCloud or Google.
  • Lightning Address: Users get a customizable @breez.tips address to share and instantly receive bitcoin.
  • Integrated On-ramps: Users can onboard to bitcoin instantly via Cash App and MoonPay. Sats arrive in seconds.
  • Contacts: Users can save their friends’ Lightning addresses, synced across devices.
  • Stable Balance: Users can avoid bitcoin’s volatility by holding a balance in USD, earn sats as they do, while still sending and receiving with BTC.
  • Send USDT/USDC: Send stablecoins from a bitcoin balance to 30+ networks (receive is coming in Q3 2026).

Developers can take these parts and deploy them to improve their apps. Building a social media app? Contacts are already there. Building a neobanking app? Stablecoins and a USD balance (with interest!) are an API call away. Travel app to simplify cross-border payments? Go for it. Building an app in a vertical the world hasn’t even thought of and need a way to let users move money anywhere for maximum global scale? What are you waiting for?

Try Glow to see how simple it is, and then explore the API to see how it connects to the SDK. Once you see how easy it is, the rest is up to you.

And since you’ll never be taking possession of users’ money, the regulatory footprint is minimal, so you can focus on building.

A Better Bitcoin Experience for Everyone

Bitcoin has finally crossed a threshold. Adding it to any app or service is now just a few lines of code: the Breez SDK has absorbed the complexities developers used to face with bitcoin, helping product teams deliver a world-class UX for millions globally.

Literally any product, from a neobank to a social app, can now empower users to move value instantly, anywhere, and directly. It took us years to perfect this; now it takes just minutes to add it to your app.

Glow is your head start. It’s open-source, as a PWA and now as a native app, and it can be white-labeled: fork it, rebrand it, ship it as your own.

Bitcoin can now surpass the UX of everyday banking and payment apps, and the DX gets you there so fast it almost feels like cheating.

Glow is now available to download on the App Store and Google Play.

To learn more visit: https://breez.technology/glow/

item.title: Breez x Turnkey: Instant Bitcoin for Embedded Wallets
item.dc:creator: Danny S
item.content:encoded:
Bringing bitcoin to millions means meeting people where they are. For users, that’s money that moves like the apps they already know. For developers, it’s bitcoin that fits the product they’ve already built. Our latest update is for the latter.

Many mainstream apps run everything from the backend, with one service handling millions of users. As a result, adding bitcoin for these teams generally means holding keys on their servers, and holding keys makes you a custodian: licenses, liability, and a honeypot that never sleeps. The alternative is creating a separate experience or rebuilding the product around a device-based wallet, sacrificing the architecture that helped them scale to millions of users in the first place.

They shouldn’t have to choose, and now they don’t have to.

Bitcoin Tools Built for Millions

Breez has partnered with Turnkey to bring instant, non-custodial bitcoin to embedded wallets. Turnkey’s enterprise-grade embedded wallet infrastructure is trusted by some of the most popular apps in the world, and the idea is simple: every user gets a wallet whose keys are created and stored inside Turnkey’s secure enclaves, where nothing can reach them. Not your server. Not Breez. Not Turnkey. Your backend holds a simple credential, and you decide exactly what it’s allowed to do.

Turnkey already supports Spark natively, and the Breez SDK is built on Spark. Pair that with Breez’s server mode and a single backend can run multi-user wallets for millions of users, all server-side managed. Instant, non-custodial bitcoin for every user, with no keys ever stored on your servers.

How It Works

For builders, the model is simple: only the user can move their money. Approval comes from a credential only they hold, like a passkey registered with Turnkey when they sign up. Your server prepares the transaction and shows exactly what will move: the amount, the fee, the destination. The user approves, and the transaction completes. Your server can never spend without them.

For users, nothing changes. Same app, same flow. There’s no seed phrase to write down and no new habit to learn. The difference is underneath: the money is actually in their control.

Bitcoin in the World’s Biggest Products

With this release, the Breez SDK now delivers the same world-class user experience at enterprise scale. It can let millions of users send and receive bitcoin instantly without holding a single key. Exchanges can automate payouts under rules their security team wrote. Fintechs can provide a non-custodial bitcoin service with the same level of UX their users are used to.

And the infrastructure underneath was built for it: Turnkey signs instantly, is SOC 2 audited, and secures some of the world’s most popular apps.

The Breez SDK exists to put bitcoin in every app, and to make value move like information, instantly, globally, to anyone. Piece by piece, the barriers keep falling. Passkey Login replaced the seed phrase. Stable Balance took away the volatility. Send USDT/USDC connected bitcoin to the networks where dollars move. Turnkey partnership gives the world’s biggest products the simplest way to securely offer instant bitcoin and stablecoins to millions of users without taking custody of a single sat.

Instant, non-custodial bitcoin at enterprise scale is now, quite literally, turnkey. (Sorry, we had to.)

Turnkey support is live now for every team building with the Breez SDK, everything you need to get started is in our documentation.

item.title: The Breez SDK: Class of Q2 2026
item.dc:creator: Danny S
item.content:encoded:
Class is back in session, and the sixth cohort might be the most eclectic yet. Since the first roundup in Q1 2025, the lineup of apps adding instant bitcoin with the Breez SDK has grown in size and in the diverse ways they improve users’ lives.

Every team came to us with its own challenge: the user experience, the developer experience, or the speed of implementation. They keep arriving at the same conclusion: when you want instant, non-custodial bitcoin inside an app or service, without holding anyone’s funds or running infrastructure, the Breez SDK is the way to go.

This quarter spans a calorie tracker, a pixel-art world, an app that identifies wildlife from a single photo, a payments network reaching across three continents, and the biggest bitcoin-only social network on the planet. One SDK, endless possibilities. Here’s your Class of Q2 2026:

Agicash

Spend bitcoin on what you actually need

Agicash is built for living on bitcoin. Buy a gift card from your favorite merchant, then scan to spend it at the register with zero fees and no card networks in between, or send it to anyone via text or email for them to redeem. Underneath the gift cards is a non-custodial bitcoin wallet powered by the Breez SDK, so the keys stay with the user while the experience stays as simple as any payment app.

AGNT|HODL

Built for hodlers, not traders

AGNT|HODL is a non-custodial bitcoin app for hodlers, not traders. Where most apps nudge you to track the charts, AGNT|HODL is built to help you accumulate a reserve and leave it to grow. When the moment comes to actually spend, the Breez SDK moves your bitcoin instantly. Hold with discipline, grow with intent.

Alignment

Get fit, pay 30% less

Getting in shape is hard enough without overpaying for the app that helps you do it. Alignment is an all-in-one iOS app to track calories, log workouts, and build better habits. Instead of selling the service using the App Store, it lets you unlock a cheaper rate by paying in bitcoin, with no Apple tax baked into the price. The savings go straight back to users as a ~30% discount. Better habits for less, powered by the Breez SDK.

Blink

The everyday bitcoin app puts users in control

Blink is the wallet that grew out of Bitcoin Beach, the El Zonte experiment that proved a whole town could run on bitcoin. That obsession with simplicity made it the everyday choice for circular economies from Brazil to Kenya. It launched as a custodial wallet in 2020 because nothing else was simple enough for a first-timer, but custody has a ceiling. The Breez SDK removed it: the same effortless app and the same tiny payments that survive a dropped signal and never expire, except users never have to relinquish control of their own funds anymore.

Bringin

A European bank account that runs on instant bitcoin

Bringin gives Europeans everything they expect from a bank: a Visa debit card, a personal vIBAN, and SEPA Instant, all tied to a non-custodial bitcoin balance and a single login. It’s live in 28 countries, and users have moved over 170 BTC through the app. This quarter the team migrated its entire user base from the Liquid to the Spark implementation of the Breez SDK, dropping sending costs by around 70% and cutting settlement times from up to fifteen seconds down to about two. The migration was invisible to users, but the lower costs and faster transactions won’t be.

Chess Tattoo

Live chess broadcasts on Nostr, with bitcoin built in

Chess Tattoo is an AI-native chess platform where anyone can play, learn, compete, and even create entirely new games. Design your own board, universe, and pieces with AI, learn from AI grandmasters, and compete in tournaments against players from around the world. Every game is published live to Nostr, where moves, commentary, and analysis become part of an open, permanent record. Instant bitcoin powered by the Breez SDK lets players support creators and opponents in real time, with community rewards coming soon.

Club Orange

The world’s biggest bitcoin-only social network goes non-custodial

Club Orange runs the largest bitcoin-only social network in the world: 20,000+ members across 71 countries, a merchant directory, and proximity zapping that lets you send sats to anyone nearby. They started with custodial deposits back in 2022 to keep things simple, but holding other people’s bitcoin at that scale was never going to last. Moving to the Breez SDK future-proofed the network overnight: the migration happened automatically, balances carried over, and sending limits evaporated. Same meetups, same merchants, same map. The only difference is that every member now holds their own keys.

IbisWallet

A wallet built by a power user, for power users

IbisWallet is a non-custodial bitcoin wallet for people who want control: customizable, private by default, with Tor built in. The developer built it for himself, then found plenty of others who were after the same thing. The Breez SDK handles the bitcoin, so the team can focus on what sets IbisWallet apart: a clean, private app for people who know exactly what they want from a wallet.

Nostr District

A pixel-art world where bitcoin moves as freely as you do

Nostr District is a social pixel-art world built on Nostr, where people chat, customize avatars, earn and buy items, and send bitcoin to each other. Think of it as a little online universe with value transfer baked in that’s already pulling players back night after night. Powered by the Breez SDK, the sats move as freely as the avatars do.

SpecieSnapp

Point, shoot, identify, and pay by the photo

Aim your camera at a plant, an animal, a fungus, or an insect, and SpecieSnapp tells you what it is. No typing, no accounts, no sign-up. You see the exact cost up front and pay per identification from your own balance, often a fraction of a cent, with the personal data stripped from your photo before it ever leaves the phone. It turns out satisfying your curiosity costs about a sat, and the Breez SDK is what makes paying that little, that often, feel like nothing at all.

SQRIL

Scan, pay, done, across emerging markets

SQRIL is a scan-to-pay QR code payments API for emerging markets. Walk up to a local QR code anywhere across Asia, Africa, or Latin America, scan, and pay. Built on the Breez SDK, it came out of stealth in January and already covers 11 countries, with plans to reach 25+ by the end of 2026 and 45+ next year. The result: any Lightning wallet can now spend bitcoin at millions of merchants across emerging markets.

Tapnob

Receive bitcoin straight to your bank account, instantly

Tapnob helps people across Africa spend bitcoin and stablecoins by settling payments straight into local bank accounts. Its newest feature, Tapnob Addresses, lets users receive bitcoin through a Lightning Address directly into their bank, with no exchanges, no P2P trades, and no crypto infrastructure to manage. Powered by the Breez SDK, it turns bitcoin into something users can actually spend anywhere. Starting in Nigeria, the rest of the continent is close behind.

Unify

Bitcoin without the seed-phrase anxiety

Unify set out to remove the scariest parts of holding bitcoin. There’s no seed phrase to scribble down, just a one-tap encrypted cloud backup that restores on any device. Payments are Lightning-fast, and you can pay people nearby over Bluetooth, with no QR codes or addresses to copy. It’s open source, non-custodial, and powered by the Breez SDK, proving that holding your own keys doesn’t have to feel like a risk.

The Breez SDK: Class of Q2 2026 was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Send Dollars Anywhere, Straight From Bitcoin: Introducing Send USDT/USDC
item.dc:creator: Danny S
item.content:encoded:
Some time in 2025, stablecoins’ transaction volume quietly passed Visa and Mastercard combined. Around 33 trillion dollars settled on-chain last year, and the overwhelming majority of it was dollars, USDC and USDT moving across Ethereum, Solana, Tron, and a dozen other networks.

Bitcoin watched most of these dollar-denominated transactions move from the sidelines. That’s not for any failing of its own; it’s the largest asset in crypto and the soundest money in the room, but the dollars were somewhere else, on networks it could not reach. So if you were building an app where people held bitcoin, you could not easily let them send to someone who lives on dollars, like a freelancer who invoices in USDC on Base, a supplier who’s paid in USDT on Tron, or a relative who keeps savings in stablecoins.

For developers, that meant supporting separate bitcoin and stablecoin balances, just so their users could move dollars. But, finally, that’s changed.

Introducing Send USDT/USDC for the Breez SDK.

What It Does

Now, any builder can let their users send USDC or USDT straight from a bitcoin balance on practically any network the recipient already uses. Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Solana, Tron, and many more from a growing list of over 30 networks. The balance stays in bitcoin, until the moment you send, with no second network for the app or its users to manage.

If an app offers Stable Balance, users can hold dollars instead and send from that just the same. Whether they hold bitcoin or dollars, it really doesn’t matter: the app lets people send dollars anywhere either way.

How It Works

When a user enters the recipient’s address, the Breez SDK detects the address type, finds a route to deliver dollars there, and shows exactly what will arrive before the user confirms. The amount, the network, the fee — all of it visible up front.

Underneath, conversions route through our launch providers, Flashnet and Boltz. The architecture is open, so more providers can plug in over time while the goal stays the same: the cheapest, fastest conversion without taking custody. And for the user, it’s instant and non-custodial. They see bitcoin go out and dollars arrive on the network they asked for.

A user with dollars in Cash App can instantly fund their bitcoin balance, and it converts instantly to USDT on any network they choose. It doesn’t require a stablecoin issued on Lightning: the dollars stay where they already live, and bitcoin reaches them where they are. Lightning is the common language that makes bitcoin interoperable with everything.

Why This Matters

A mom can send money to her kids who hold dollars on Tron. A freelancer who saves in bitcoin can pay collaborators who only take USDC. A neobank can offer bitcoin without limiting users’ ability to pay across other networks. Until now, serving any of them meant integrating additional blockchains.

Now it’s a few lines of code for developers. Apps can let users hold what they want, bitcoin or dollars, and pay anyone on any network, non-custodially, instantly, and across any border without asking permission.

For developers, integration is straightforward, and everything you need to get started is in the Breez SDK documentation.

The Walls Keep Coming Down

The Breez SDK exists to put bitcoin in every app, and to make value move like information, instantly, globally, to anyone. For that to happen, bitcoin has to work in the products we already use. Passkey Login replaced the seed phrase. Instant onboarding with Cash App removed the wait. Stable Balance took away the volatility. Send USDT/USDC tears down the wall that kept bitcoin shut out of the networks where the world’s dollars actually change hands.

Today this is for sending only, but receiving dollars from any network is coming soon. Our reference app Glow is already running it, and it is live now for every team building with the Breez SDK. Bitcoin can finally follow users into the dollar economy, every network where the dollars move, without ever leaving bitcoin to get there. One of the last walls between bitcoin and everyday money just came down.

Send Dollars Anywhere, Straight From Bitcoin: Introducing Send USDT/USDC was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Volatility Optional: Introducing Stable Balance for the Breez SDK
item.dc:creator: Danny S
item.content:encoded:
In October 2025, bitcoin hit an all-time high of $126,000. By February, it had shed nearly half its value. None of that was bitcoin’s doing. Thank tariff wars, oil prices, and shifting monetary policy. The world moved, and bitcoin moved with it. That’s simply how decentralized price discovery in a free market works. But knowing why it happens doesn’t help when your balance is down 30%.

Of course, none of this matters much if you’re holding bitcoin for the long term. But if you’re trying to spend it today, or a merchant is trying to price a product this afternoon, that kind of movement is a big headache. It’s why many people still reach for dollars, euros, and stablecoins when they need their money to sit still.

Volatility is one of the biggest remaining barriers preventing bitcoin from being adopted as everyday money. It’s hard to spend or budget with a balance that’s constantly moving.

Stable Balance changes that.

What It Does

Stable Balance is a new feature of the Breez SDK that lets users hold their balance in USD. When a user receives bitcoin, the SDK automatically converts the incoming sats to dollars. When they send bitcoin, it converts back to sats on the fly. The user sees a dollar balance that holds its value, and they can still send and receive bitcoin just like always.

No new wallets, no extra steps. Users can toggle Stable Balance on or off at will. Turn it on, and incoming sats convert to USD automatically. Turn it off, and the dollar balance converts back to bitcoin. That’s it. When developers enable the feature, conversions happen quietly in the background.

How It Works

The dollar balance is backed by USDB, a stablecoin issued by Brale and native to Spark.

When a conversion needs to happen, the SDK routes it through Flashnet, a decentralized exchange built on Spark. The Breez SDK handles the rest, managing each conversion from start to finish so developers don’t have to. None of this complexity surfaces to the user. They just see a dollar balance that stays where it should.

As a bonus, holding USDB earns yield paid daily in bitcoin, with no lockups or extra steps required. The full details are in Spark’s USDB documentation. But the core value proposition is as simple as can be: a user’s $50 balance is still worth $50 tomorrow.

Why This Matters

A user sending remittances to loved ones cannot afford a 5% swing between deposit and withdrawal. A freelancer invoicing in bitcoin doesn’t want to worry about what the dollar equivalent will be when rent is due. A neobank integrating bitcoin wants to offer stability to users who think in their local currency.

While traditional banking and payment apps offer stable balances, your money remains stuck in that system. Frozen accounts, blocked payment pathways, and withdrawal limits are all structural trade-offs that shape any user experience built on top of them. Stable Balance in the Breez SDK combines the, well, stable balance of tradfi apps with the freedom to move value instantly, across any border, without depending on anyone in between.

Stable Balance also meets users where they are. It doesn’t ask anyone to change how they think about money. It gives them a dollar-denominated balance that rides on bitcoin’s rails, all while preserving the speed, cost structure, and non-custodial properties of the Breez SDK.

For developers, integration is straightforward. Stable Balance takes a few lines of code to configure and is available in all major languages and frameworks. Everything you need to get started is in our Breez SDK documentation.

The Future of Bitcoin UX Is Here

Every feature the Breez SDK ships is in service of the same goal: bitcoin in every app. And to make that happen, bitcoin must work for real users in everyday products. Passkey Login removed the need for a seed phrase. Stable Balance removes the price volatility. Piece by piece, we’re tearing down the barriers that stood between bitcoin and everyday use.

Our reference app Glow is already running Stable Balance, and it’s available now for every developer building with the Breez SDK. Price volatility was one of the last major UX barriers standing between bitcoin and the mainstream. Now it’s optional.

Volatility Optional: Introducing Stable Balance for the Breez SDK was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: The Breez SDK: Class of Q1 2026
item.dc:creator: Danny S
item.content:encoded:
The first class of SDK partners we introduced was Q1 2025, making this the fifth entry. While it’s still too early to say where this trend is headed, we can safely say it’s a trend.

Each of these partners has come to the Breez SDK on their own path, but their reasons tend to overlap. Whether you look at the user experience, the developer experience, the ease of implementation, the cost, the support, or any other criterion, it’s hard to find a better way to add instant, non-custodial bitcoin to any app or service. We’re constantly adding new features, like passkey login, and we prioritize our own development pipeline based on what our partners tell us they need.

Perhaps the most thrilling aspect of reviewing the latest cohort of new partners or, indeed, the dozens of partners who’ve implemented the Breez SDK so far, is just how diverse they are. Once again in this class, we have pure crypto ventures, messaging apps, loyalty programs for retailers, savings apps, and even cooking.

It just goes to show that the Breez SDK is as scalable as it is versatile. Check it out:

BAOMarkets

A bitcoin-based prediction market you can bet on

Like Bitcoin itself, the idea of prediction markets has been around for a long time, just waiting for the right technology. And just as Lightning and Breez have been revolutionizing what bitcoin can do, BAOMarkets is leveraging this dynamic duo to revolutionize what prediction markets can do. In fact, the Breez SDK is what makes long-term bets possible by letting them book bets that extend beyond Lightning’s 24-hour HTLCs without losing custody and final settlement. Innovation like that is always a safe bet.

BitLasso

Built-in volume discounts for retailers and service providers of all kinds

Regular customers are golden because the cost of customer acquisition is such a drag. BitLasso helps vendors of all kinds turn their customers into regulars by letting vendors issue customers with tokens for each paid invoice that the customers can redeem for discounts on future purchases. The more you buy, the more you save. Now with the Breez SDK, those customer payments are even faster, but just as final and non-custodial as ever.

Cake Wallet

An old friend comes back for seconds

Cake first implemented the Breez SDK based on Greenlight back in 2024. Now, after two years of learning and refining, they’re back to take advantage of the newer Spark implementation. It’s even easier for their devs to work with, and simplifies life on the users’ end too. We love growing together with Cake, and we’re eager to see where our common road leads next.

Deblock

A European neobank giving sovereignty to the masses

Deblock is on a mission to combine the ease of conventional banking with the sovereignty of crypto. Once they had jumped through the regulatory hoops of operating a bank in Europe, they turned to the daunting task of integrating bitcoin. But it was only daunting until they found the Breez SDK, which made bitcoin transfers faster, cheaper, and simpler than they or their users had thought possible.

Evento

Bringing people together through fun and bitcoin

Having lived through the pandemic, we all understand isolation and alienation. Evento is an antidote to both, helping people to build communities by organizing events. Users can sell tickets, raise money through crowdfunding, and find each other on the global bitcoin events map. And it’s all peer-to-peer. Evento is exactly the kind of activity we built Breez to support, and that’s why they also won one of the top prizes in our recent </time2build> developer challenge.

Exolix

Aggregating exchanges to get users the best deal

Once upon a time, there were only a few coins out there and only a few exchanges to trade them on. With over 14K coins now spread across over 27K exchanges, how do you know you’re getting the best deal? Exolix is constantly scanning the market for the best rates. Users can send their orders and receive their funds within minutes at the cheapest rates available on nearly 1700 exchanges. And they now move bitcoin Lightning-fast with the Breez SDK.

Primal

Nostr messaging with built-in bitcoin value transfer

Nostr is a messaging technology built on the same principles as Bitcoin and Lightning: decentralization, peer-to-peer interaction, personal sovereignty, and freedom. Primal is a Nostr client that reflects those same principles, but they were facing the same dilemma as everyone else. Either they could use a custodial solution, with all the regulatory and counterparty risk that entails, or they could build their own Lightning client, punishing their users and devs in the process. The Breez SDK lets them combine the best of both worlds: a UX and DX with the sovereignty and freedom that Bitcoin and Nostr were built on.

kute wallet

The all-in-one wallet goes all-in with the Breez SDK

kute wallet is for people who want all the benefits in a single package. It lets users hold their funds, connect with their hardwallets, use their phones as air-gapped signers, and buy bitcoin without KYC. Oh, and they can trade on Polymarket too. So it makes perfect sense that the do-everything wallet has the Breez SDK running on both the Spark and Liquid implementations. If some is good, more has to be better.

Swaptrade

Swapping bitcoin just got a lot faster

Swaptrade is a non-custodial swapping platform that is all about user choice. As nice as it is to be able to swap between 11 different coins without losing custody, bitcoin swaps were, until recently, slow. Without Lightning, Swaptrade users had to wait for on-chain confirmation. With the Breez SDK, their funds move magically in seconds for fast and secure swaps. The Breez SDK lets them increase their throughput while decreasing users’ wait times.

Sweep

Automating savings with the best asset in existence

Passive income is an elusive goal that many strive to achieve. Sweep has achieved the next best thing: automating savings with bitcoin. Users can connect Sweep to their bank accounts (without Sweep seeing their account details), spend normally from their bank account on whatever purchases they like, and Sweep rounds the total up as defined by the user, automatically investing the change in bitcoin. A single father developed this to teach his two teenage girls about saving, but he might have been too successful. If saving is this easy, they’ll never have to think about it.

Wisp

Social media rebuilt on open protocols and instant bitcoin

Wisp is a Nostr client that refuses to compromise. No ads, no algorithms, no corporate ownership, and now, no friction on bitcoin either. With the Breez SDK, Wisp onboards every user to instant, non-custodial bitcoin automatically, no wallet setup required. The result is one of the smoothest zapping experiences on Nostr today. Six weeks after launch, Wisp had already cracked the top five Nostr clients, and users can even cash out to Bitrefill without leaving the app.

Zap Cooking

Send your compliments to the chef in bitcoin

Zap Cooking is another app leveraging Nostr that lets users share recipes, cooking tips, and products while tipping each other for spreading the joy of delicious meals and treats. It’s a simple idea that builds community based on shared interests. The Breez SDK just facilitates the tokens of appreciation that these like-minded gourmets relish.

The Breez SDK: Class of Q1 2026 was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: No Seed, No Sweat: Introducing Passkey Login for the Breez SDK
item.dc:creator: Roy Sheinfeld
item.content:encoded:
For as long as bitcoin wallets have existed, the seed phrase has been both a superpower and a liability. Those 12 or 24 words are the master key to your funds. Write them down, keep them safe, never lose them, never let anyone see them. Definitely do not save them to a hard drive, toss the hard drive into the trash, and then spend millions trying to get them back out before giving up, sad and much poorer.

It’s stories like this that scare so many potential users away from self-custody. A sticky note in a drawer, a screenshot in iCloud, a forgotten notebook. There are so many simple ways to blow this one crucial step, but the consequences are permanent.

The rest of the tech industry has been moving away from passwords for years. The stakes with bitcoin are higher, but the logic is the same. It’s time Bitcoin caught up.

The Missing Piece: PRF

Passkeys aren’t new. Apple, Google, and Microsoft jointly backed the standard in 2022, and the market has welcomed the move enthusiastically. According to the FIDO Alliance, over a billion people have activated at least one passkey, and as of May 2025, 69% of users have set one up. 48% of the top 100 websites now support them. They’re built into every modern phone and computer. The technology is proven. Bitcoin just hasn’t adopted it yet.

The missing piece was key derivation. Passkeys are great for authentication, but a bitcoin wallet needs to deterministically derive cryptographic keys, not just match a user with their account. Bitcoin presents a different problem, and until recently there was no standard way to solve it.

That’s what the PRF extension of WebAuthn solves, and it’s the key ingredient in Passkey Login. PRF is a newer capability, part of the WebAuthn Level 3 spec, that lets your passkey produce a deterministic cryptographic output for any given input. Same passkey, same input, same output. Always. The passkey never leaves your device’s secure enclave.

PRF is what separates passkeys-for-authentication from passkeys-for-key-derivation. Regular passkeys can verify who you are. PRF lets them generate secrets deterministically.

PRF support is still rolling out unevenly across various platforms. Android with Google Password Manager has the most complete support. Apple added PRF in iOS 18 and macOS 15 for iCloud Keychain. Windows Hello doesn’t support PRF at all yet, so only external hardware keys like YubiKeys work on Windows. Firefox support is also incomplete. It works well on Android and increasingly on Apple platforms, but not everywhere.

Logging in to the Breez SDK with a passkey requires PRF, so coverage today maps to where PRF works. As adoption grows (and it’s growing fast!), so does the utility.

The practical result: any device with a PRF-capable passkey can reconstruct your wallet keys from scratch and on demand.

How It Works

Your Passkey Derives Your Keys

When you set up Passkey Login, the app uses your passkey to compute a PRF output. That output becomes the root key for your wallet. From there, standard key derivation produces keys for the Breez SDK.

No randomness is stored. No backup is created. The passkey is the key generator, and it only works when you authenticate. The protocol also supports multiple wallets, each derived from a different label.

Nostr Keeps Track of Your Labels

Here’s where Nostr comes in, but not as a core security primitive. Instead, Nostr is a practical solution to a real problem: if your keys are derived from labels, how do you remember which labels you used when restoring on a new device?

The answer is to publish them. Under the hood, the app seamlessly creates a Nostr identity derived from the same PRF and uses it to post each label as a plain Nostr event. The user never sees or manages this identity. When you restore, the app reconstructs that same Nostr identity, queries the relays, retrieves the list of labels, and re-derives the keys on the spot.

No cloud backup. No iCloud. No Google Drive. No server. Just your passkey and a few public Nostr messages.

Trust and Tradeoffs

The app stores nothing. Keys are derived fresh on every use, with no local secrets and no encrypted backup file. There is a soft dependency on Nostr relays for label lookup, though Breez handles all of this out of the box.

The security is as strong as your passkey. If your passkey is cloud-synced, as most platform passkeys are, a compromised cloud account means compromised keys. And if you lose access to your passkey entirely, you lose access to your funds.

Passkeys also aren’t fully interoperable across platforms yet. That’s why the Breez SDK lets you export the mnemonic for any of your wallets. If you ever need to move to a platform or wallet that doesn’t support passkeys, you have a standard seed phrase to fall back on.

Why This Matters

The seed phrase has been a barrier to self-custody since day one. It’s what scares normies away from keeping their own bitcoin, and it’s a legitimate reason why people accept the counterparty risk of exchanges and custodial apps.

Passkey Login doesn’t eliminate the tradeoffs of self-custody, but it reframes them around something people already understand and use, namely the same biometric authentication that protects their banking app and their password manager. For most users, that’s a much more intuitive security model than a piece of paper in a drawer.

For developers building on the Breez SDK, it means onboarding without the “write down these 12 words before you continue” speed bump, while still giving users full control over their keys.

The Future of Bitcoin UX Is Here

The full technical specification for Passkey Login is public, and our reference app Glow is already running it, and it’s now available for all the Breez SDK devs to use.

The seed phrase has been one of the biggest UX barriers to bitcoin adoption, but we finally have the tools to overcome it. Passkey Login builds on authentication infrastructure that billions of people already use every day, and it makes using bitcoin feel as natural as unlocking your phone. That’s what drives the Breez SDK: pushing the boundaries of what’s possible until yesterday’s Bitcoin dreams become today’s reality.

No Seed, No Sweat: Introducing Passkey Login for the Breez SDK was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Lightning Is Dead, Long Live Lightning!
item.dc:creator: Roy Sheinfeld
item.content:encoded:
Lightning continues to evolve, but most of the changes we’ve witnessed over the last decade are changes in the technology. What’s happened over the last two years, however, is a change of the technology. We’re not talking about protocol enhancements or new features, but a fundamental reconceptualization of what Lightning is, what it can do, and who uses it for what.

We’ve discussed some of these changes before in isolation, but they can be a little abstract. That’s why we tend to use metaphors like “common language” and “last-mile technology.”

Fortunately, one of our partners, Cake Wallet, has traced this path with us, and their story renders the abstraction of Lightning’s recent transformation marvelously concrete. So let me tell you the story of Lightning, Breez, and Cake.

If We Only Node Then What We Know Now

In 2024, we at Breez were very glad to welcome Cake as an early design partner using our (then) brand-new SDK. Cake implemented the Breez SDK using Greenlight in their wallet. While Greenlight’s remote nodes improved the Lightning UX relative to client nodes running on users’ phones, Cake never put it into production, and we have since deprecated it.

Greenlight was a quality-of-life improvement over earlier implementations of Lightning on mobile devices. Running an actual Lightning node on users’ phones devoured resources and required constant sync with the Bitcoin chain and the Lightning Network, which was very challenging to solve with the restrictions of the contemporary mobile operating systems. By moving users’ nodes into the cloud and shifting many of the moving parts into the background, Greenlight did improve the UX.

However, even with Greenlight, compromises between open, permissionless, borderless Bitcoin and an intuitive, frictionless UX remained. For example, liquidity remained a tough nut to crack for everyone involved. Receiving bitcoin offline still required improvised workarounds using mobile notifications. We thought that Greenlight was the best balance available at the time, comparable in custody and openness with its predecessors and surpassing them in simplicity, but the UX was still too complicated and Greenlight itself proved hard to scale.

It’s for reasons like these that Cake never took the Greenlight implementation of the Breez SDK into production, despite praising its design, simplicity, and functionality. Greenlight was an advance in the technology, but Lightning needed a fundamental change of the technology.

Cake tried the Greenlight solution, and it turned out to be good enough for devs but still lacking for users. They opted not to compromise and rather wait for a better product. And honestly, that’s exactly the feedback we needed.

A Common Language for the Last Mile

Times change, and tech changes with them.

More specifically, several last-mile technologies have emerged to improve the experience of the world’s Bitcoin users and the economics of moving bitcoin. These include new-gen statechains like Spark, sidechains like Liquid, federations for friends and family like Fedimint, eCash networks like Cashu, and advanced programming layers like Arkade. They’re all variations on a common theme: just as Lightning improves on Bitcoin’s economics and throughput, these last-mile technologies all improve on Lightning’s payment channels, economics, complexity, and scalability.

Lightning is still a vital part of how we transfer value, but it has evolved to become the common language and payment protocol that connects these last-mile technologies rather than a channels protocol that end users need to master. And Lightning’s connections run deep. Even when bitcoin moves from a Spark entity to Arkade or between a Fedimint federation and Liquid, those various subnetworks speak to each other in fluent Lightning.

Lightning’s transformation seems inevitable to anyone who understands the economics of Lightning and values UX. Poon-Dryja payment channels excel when there’s a constant flow of high-velocity transactions, especially when they’re bi-directional. Even if problems that inherently stem from mobile usage (such as network synchronization and offline receive) are solved, edge nodes will always under-perform at low transaction velocities. Liquidity management and economics is a feature for routing nodes, but a bug when it comes to end-user nodes. Luckily, these last-mile technologies solve such issues and other UX complexities, and with Lightning as the common language that connects them, Bitcoin just works for devs and users alike.

The Return of Cake

Talking about the evolution of Lightning is so exciting, I almost forgot to tell you the big news: Cake Wallet is now taking the Breez SDK into production! Huzzah!

Cake continued to research the Bitcoin-UX dilemma and explore various last-mile solutions. The Spark implementation of the Breez SDK provided Cake with a balanced trade-off between a trust-minimized solution and the UX they deserve. It combines the openness, utility, and finality of bitcoin with features that have eluded Lightning until now, like offline payments.

And the UX, which used to be the weak spot, is now the best part. Payments are instant. Offline payments and Lightning addresses are built in. Fees are infinitesimal. Like any fintech app, the complexity behind the scenes is substantial but irrelevant, because users just see money moving where they want, when they want, how they want. It’s bitcoin as digital cash. Users get to have their Cake and eat it too (sorry, I had to).

Of course, we haven’t compromised on the developer experience, which is better than ever. The API of the Breez SDK is designed by developers for developers to be as simple as possible with clear, extensive instructions and rapid, helpful support. With a user-friendly product, Cake is serving its end users, and with a developer-friendly product, we’re serving Cake’s product team.

Lightning Grows When We Cultivate It Together

Breez was among the first to see the promise of Lightning and ship a functional mobile app, but our users pushed us to build a better experience. We worked together with the Blockstream team, who devised Greenlight, to optimize it for users and developers alike. Again, we were proud and with good reason, because our old Greenlight SDK was a significant improvement. But partners like Cake weren’t yet satisfied despite giving the Greenlight implementation a fair chance. They pushed us to build better.

We have, and by “we” I mean the whole Lightning community. Breez is still working with Blockstream on the Liquid implementation of the SDK, and we’re working with Lightspark on the Spark implementation, leveraging it to provide the best-in-class Lightning experience

This is exactly how it’s supposed to work. We build as far as we can with existing technology, and then we release the result out into the market to raise the bar and to determine where we still need to improve. Dedicated partners like Cake tell us how by sharing what they and their users need. Then we meet with our allies who are pursuing the same goal, and we cooperate to build the next miracle and reach the next optimum.

The story of Breez, Lightning, and Cake holds two lessons. First, there’s no alternative but to keep building and testing. Second, even though it’s impossible to tell what the next innovation in Lightning will be or how it will perform, the overall trajectory is obvious: Lightning keeps getting better. It’s now a much more functional technology helping far more people do far more things than it was when we all started.

Don’t you love a story with a happy ending?

Lightning Is Dead, Long Live Lightning! was originally published in Breez on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.
